claim: Parkinson's disease-associated LRRK2 kinase phosphorylates multiple Rab GTPases, including Rab8A and Rab10.
source: Parkinson's disease-associated LRRK2 kinase phosphorylates multiple Rab GTPases, including Rab8A and Rab10.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work (Steger et al., 2016; Steger et al., 2017) mentioned in the Introduction section.

claim: LRRK2 kinase interferes with primary cilia formation in cultured cells.
source: We show here that LRRK2 kinase interferes with primary cilia formation in cultured cells, human LRRK2 G2019S iPS cells and in the cortex of LRRK2 R1441C mice.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 6, 7, and 8, demonstrating reduced ciliation in cells expressing pathogenic LRRK2.

claim: LRRK2 kinase interferes with primary cilia formation in human LRRK2 G2019S iPS cells.
source: We show here that LRRK2 kinase interferes with primary cilia formation in cultured cells, human LRRK2 G2019S iPS cells and in the cortex of LRRK2 R1441C mice.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7B-D, demonstrating reduced ciliation in G2019S iPS cells compared to corrected controls.

claim: LRRK2 kinase interferes with primary cilia formation in the cortex of LRRK2 R1441C mice.
source: We show here that LRRK2 kinase interferes with primary cilia formation in cultured cells, human LRRK2 G2019S iPS cells and in the cortex of LRRK2 R1441C mice.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8A-D, demonstrating reduced ciliation in the cortex of R1441C mice.

claim: Rab10 phosphorylation strengthens its intrinsic ability to block ciliogenesis by enhancing binding to RILPL1.
source: Rab10 phosphorylation strengthens its intrinsic ability to block ciliogenesis by enhancing binding to RILPL1.
evidence: This claim is supported by data in Figures 3, 4, and 6 showing enhanced RILPL1 binding to phosphorylated Rab10 and the requirement of both proteins for LRRK2-mediated ciliation defects.

claim: The ability of LRRK2 to interfere with ciliogenesis requires both Rab10 and RILPL1 proteins.
source: Importantly, the ability of LRRK2 to interfere with ciliogenesis requires both Rab10 and RILPL1 proteins.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data in Figure 6C showing that depletion of either Rab10 or RILPL1 abolishes the effect of LRRK2-R1441G on cilia formation.

claim: Pathogenic LRRK2 influences the ability of cells to respond to cilia-dependent, Hedgehog signaling as monitored by Gli1 transcriptional activation.
source: Pathogenic LRRK2 influences the ability of cells to respond to cilia-dependent, Hedgehog signaling as monitored by Gli1 transcriptional activation.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data in Figure 7A and 7E showing reduced Gli1 expression in LRRK2 mutant cells and restoration upon LRRK2 inhibition.

claim: Cholinergic neurons in the striatum of LRRK2 R1441C mice show decreased ciliation.
source: Moreover, cholinergic neurons in the striatum of LRRK2 R1441C mice show decreased ciliation, which will decrease their ability to sense Sonic hedgehog in a neuro-protective circuit that supports dopaminergic neurons.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data in Figure 8E-F showing significantly reduced ciliation in ChAT-positive neurons in R1441C striatum.

claim: Decreased ciliation in cholinergic neurons will decrease their ability to sense Sonic hedgehog in a neuro-protective circuit that supports dopaminergic neurons.
source: Moreover, cholinergic neurons in the striatum of LRRK2 R1441C mice show decreased ciliation, which will decrease their ability to sense Sonic hedgehog in a neuro-protective circuit that supports dopaminergic neurons.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the observed ciliation defects and established knowledge about Shh signaling requiring cilia, combined with citation to Gonzalez-Reyes et al., 2012.

claim: Autosomal dominant mutations in the LRRK2 gene account for 1–2% of all Parkinson's disease cases.
source: Although the cause of most Parkinson's disease remains unknown, autosomal dominant mutations in the leucine rich repeat kinase 2 (LRRK2) gene account for 1–2% of all cases (and 18% of cases in those of Ashkenazi Jewish descent) and lead to activation of the LRRK2 kinase (Alessi and Sammler, 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Alessi and Sammler, 2018.

claim: LRRK2 mutations account for 18% of Parkinson's disease cases in those of Ashkenazi Jewish descent.
source: Although the cause of most Parkinson's disease remains unknown, autosomal dominant mutations in the leucine rich repeat kinase 2 (LRRK2) gene account for 1–2% of all cases (and 18% of cases in those of Ashkenazi Jewish descent) and lead to activation of the LRRK2 kinase (Alessi and Sammler, 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Alessi and Sammler, 2018.

claim: Autosomal dominant mutations in LRRK2 lead to activation of the LRRK2 kinase.
source: Although the cause of most Parkinson's disease remains unknown, autosomal dominant mutations in the leucine rich repeat kinase 2 (LRRK2) gene account for 1–2% of all cases (and 18% of cases in those of Ashkenazi Jewish descent) and lead to activation of the LRRK2 kinase (Alessi and Sammler, 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Alessi and Sammler, 2018.

claim: A subgroup of Rab GTPases are the primary substrates of LRRK2.
source: Recent mass spectrometry efforts have revealed a subgroup of Rab GTPases as the primary substrates of LRRK2 (Steger et al., 2016; Steger et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Steger et al., 2016 and Steger et al., 2017.

claim: Rab GTPases are master regulators of all membrane trafficking events in eukaryotic cells.
source: Rab GTPases are master regulators of all membrane trafficking events in eukaryotic cells (Wandinger-Ness and Zerial, 2014; Pfeffer, 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Wandinger-Ness and Zerial, 2014 and Pfeffer, 2017.

claim: LRRK2 phosphorylation modifies the switch 2 regions of Rab proteins.
source: LRRK2 phosphorylation modifies the so-called switch 2 regions of Rab proteins that report the identity of the bound nucleotide.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Steger et al., 2016 in the following sentence.

claim: Phosphorylation on the switch two loop interferes with the ability of Rabs to bind to most of their partner proteins.
source: Because cognate effector and regulatory proteins interact with Rabs in a nucleotide-dependent manner via this motif, phosphorylation on the switch two loop interferes with the ability of Rabs to bind to most of their partner proteins (Steger et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Steger et al., 2016.

claim: Rab29 GTPase, localized on the Golgi, recruits the predominantly cytoplasmic LRRK2 onto membranes and activates its ability to phosphorylate downstream Rab8A and Rab10 substrates.
source: We recently showed that Rab29 GTPase, localized on the Golgi, recruits the predominantly cytoplasmic LRRK2 onto membranes and activates it's ability to phosphorylate downstream Rab8A and Rab10 substrates (Purlyte et al., 2018; see also Liu et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Purlyte et al., 2018 and Liu et al., 2018.

claim: Rab8A and Rab10 have been implicated in the process of ciliogenesis.
source: Although Rab8A and Rab10 have distinct localizations and roles in different tissues, they (along with Rab29) have been implicated in the process of ciliogenesis.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to multiple papers in the following sentences.

claim: Primary cilia are single, microtubule-based cellular projections on many types of cells that are critical for developmental signaling via the Sonic hedgehog pathway.
source: Primary cilia are single, microtubule-based cellular projections on many types of cells that are critical for developmental signaling via the Sonic hedgehog (Shh) pathway as well as for G-protein coupled receptor signaling pathways; they are produced in tight coordination with the cell cycle (Hilgendorf et al., 2016; Rohatgi et al., 2007; Yoshimura et al., 2007; Nachury et al., 2007)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Hilgendorf et al., 2016; Rohatgi et al., 2007; Yoshimura et al., 2007; Nachury et al., 2007.

claim: Primary cilia are critical for G-protein coupled receptor signaling pathways.
source: Primary cilia are single, microtubule-based cellular projections on many types of cells that are critical for developmental signaling via the Sonic hedgehog (Shh) pathway as well as for G-protein coupled receptor signaling pathways; they are produced in tight coordination with the cell cycle (Hilgendorf et al., 2016; Rohatgi et al., 2007; Yoshimura et al., 2007; Nachury et al., 2007)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Hilgendorf et al., 2016; Rohatgi et al., 2007; Yoshimura et al., 2007; Nachury et al., 2007.

claim: Primary cilia are produced in tight coordination with the cell cycle.
source: Primary cilia are single, microtubule-based cellular projections on many types of cells that are critical for developmental signaling via the Sonic hedgehog (Shh) pathway as well as for G-protein coupled receptor signaling pathways; they are produced in tight coordination with the cell cycle (Hilgendorf et al., 2016; Rohatgi et al., 2007; Yoshimura et al., 2007; Nachury et al., 2007)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Hilgendorf et al., 2016; Rohatgi et al., 2007; Yoshimura et al., 2007; Nachury et al., 2007.

claim: The basal body associated, Cenexin-3 protein binds Rab8A and relocates to the primary cilium together with Rab8A upon serum starvation.
source: Yoshimura et al. (2007) also discovered that the basal body associated, Cenexin-3 protein binds Rab8A and relocates to the primary cilium together with Rab8A upon serum starvation.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Yoshimura et al., 2007.

claim: Both Rab8A and its guanine nucleotide exchange factor, Rabin8, are needed in part, for BBSome function in ciliogenesis.
source: Subsequent work has shown that both Rab8A and its guanine nucleotide exchange factor, Rabin8, are needed in part, for so-called BBSome function in ciliogenesis (Nachury et al., 2007; Knödler et al., 2010; Westlake et al., 2011; Feng et al., 2012)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Nachury et al., 2007; Knödler et al., 2010; Westlake et al., 2011; Feng et al., 2012.

claim: Rab8A and Rabin8 are needed for the delivery of membrane vesicles to the growing cilium.
source: Subsequent work has shown that both Rab8A and its guanine nucleotide exchange factor, Rabin8, are needed in part, for so-called BBSome function in ciliogenesis (Nachury et al., 2007; Knödler et al., 2010; Westlake et al., 2011; Feng et al., 2012) and also for the delivery of membrane vesicles to the growing cilium (Lu et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Lu et al., 2015.

claim: Rab10 is detected in association with primary cilia in cultured MDCK and LLC-PK1 kidney cells and in rodent renal tubules.
source: Rab10 is detected in association with primary cilia in cultured MDCK and LLC-PK1 kidney cells and in rodent renal tubules (Babbey et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Babbey et al., 2010.

claim: Rab10 is necessary for axonal membrane trafficking and axonal elongation.
source: Rab10 is also reported to be necessary for axonal membrane trafficking and axonal elongation (Wang et al., 2011; Liu et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Wang et al., 2011 and Liu et al., 2013.

claim: Rab8A and Rab10 have opposing roles in normal ciliogenesis.
source: We show here that Rab8A and Rab10 have opposing roles in normal ciliogenesis.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data in Figure 1 showing that Rab8A increases while Rab10 inhibits cilia formation.

claim: Rab10 is a native suppressor of ciliogenesis.
source: Unlike Rab8A, Rab10 is a native suppressor of ciliogenesis, and upon LRRK2 phosphorylation, it binds preferentially to RILPL1 (Rab interacting lysosomal protein-like 1) protein to further interfere with cilia formation.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data in Figures 1, 5, and 6 showing that Rab10 inhibits ciliogenesis.

claim: Upon LRRK2 phosphorylation, Rab10 binds preferentially to RILPL1 protein to further interfere with cilia formation.
source: Unlike Rab8A, Rab10 is a native suppressor of ciliogenesis, and upon LRRK2 phosphorylation, it binds preferentially to RILPL1 (Rab interacting lysosomal protein-like 1) protein to further interfere with cilia formation.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data in Figures 3, 4, and 6 showing enhanced RILPL1 binding to phosphorylated Rab10 and the requirement of both proteins for LRRK2-mediated ciliation defects.

claim: Loss of cilia will decrease the ability of cholinergic neurons to respond to a Sonic hedgehog signal that triggers neuroprotective signaling toward dopaminergic circuits.
source: These cilia modulatory events have important consequences in the brain where they influence the ability of cholinergic neurons to generate cilia in the somatosensory cortex; loss of cilia will decrease the ability of these neurons to respond to a Sonic hedgehog signal that triggers neuroprotective signaling toward dopaminergic circuits (Gonzalez-Reyes et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the observed ciliation defects and citation to Gonzalez-Reyes et al., 2012 describing the neuroprotective circuit.

claim: Some of the total pool of Rab8A localized at the base and within primary cilia.
source: Consistent with previous reports (Yoshimura et al., 2007; Nachury et al., 2007; Feng et al., 2012; Knödler et al., 2010; Sato et al., 2014; Babbey et al., 2010), some of the total pool of Rab8A localized at the base and within primary cilia (detected with anti-Arl13b antibody; Figure 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A and citations to previous reports.

claim: A portion of the total pool of Rab10 localized only to the base of cilia in both hTERT-RPE as well as primary, antibody-panned, rat astrocyte cells.
source: In contrast, a portion of the total pool of Rab10 localized only to the base of cilia in both hTERT-RPE as well as primary, antibody-panned, rat astrocyte cells (Figure 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Loss of Rab8A decreased significantly the capacity of A549 or RPE cells to generate primary cilia.
source: As shown previously, loss of Rab8A decreased significantly the capacity of A549 or RPE cells to generate primary cilia (Figure 1B–D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B-D.

claim: Loss of Rab10 increased the percentage of cells that made primary cilia compared with parental wild type A549 and RPE cells.
source: Surprisingly, loss of Rab10 increased the percentage of cells that made primary cilia compared with parental wild type A549 and RPE cells (Figure 1B,C,E).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B, C, and E.

claim: The effects of Rab8A or Rab10 knockout on primary cilia formation were reversed upon re-expression of exogenous Rab8A or Rab10 wild type proteins.
source: Importantly, the effects of Rab8A or Rab10 knockout on primary cilia formation were reversed upon re-expression of exogenous Rab8A or Rab10 wild type proteins (Figure 1D,E; Rab10,~4 fold overexpressed and Rab8A,~10 fold): exogenous Rab8A stimulated while Rab10 inhibited ciliogenesis in cells lacking these proteins.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1D and E.

claim: Exogenous Rab8A stimulated ciliogenesis in cells lacking Rab8A.
source: Importantly, the effects of Rab8A or Rab10 knockout on primary cilia formation were reversed upon re-expression of exogenous Rab8A or Rab10 wild type proteins (Figure 1D,E; Rab10,~4 fold overexpressed and Rab8A,~10 fold): exogenous Rab8A stimulated while Rab10 inhibited ciliogenesis in cells lacking these proteins.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Exogenous Rab10 inhibited ciliogenesis in cells lacking Rab10.
source: Importantly, the effects of Rab8A or Rab10 knockout on primary cilia formation were reversed upon re-expression of exogenous Rab8A or Rab10 wild type proteins (Figure 1D,E; Rab10,~4 fold overexpressed and Rab8A,~10 fold): exogenous Rab8A stimulated while Rab10 inhibited ciliogenesis in cells lacking these proteins.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: Loss of both Rab8A and Rab10 from A549 cells reversed the block of ciliogenesis observed in Rab8A KO cells.
source: Surprisingly, loss of both Rab8A and Rab10 from A549 cells reversed the block of ciliogenesis observed in Rab8A KO cells (Figure 1F).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1F.

claim: Rab10 is a dominant suppressor of cilia formation.
source: Thus, Rab10 is a dominant suppressor of cilia formation.
evidence: This claim is an inference based on the experimental data showing that loss of Rab10 rescues ciliation defects in Rab8A KO cells.

claim: Exogenous Rab8A further increases ciliation in Rab10 KO cells.
source: Even though A549 Rab10 KO cells are significantly ciliated, exogenous Rab8A even further increases ciliation in these cells (Figure 1G).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1G.

claim: Rab8A drives a Rab10-independent pathway for cilia formation.
source: Thus, Rab8A drives a Rab10-independent pathway for cilia formation.
evidence: This claim is an inference based on the experimental data showing that Rab8A can increase ciliation in Rab10 KO cells.

claim: Loss of either Rab10 or Rab8A does not change the level of the other protein.
source: Note that loss of either Rab10 or Rab8A does not change the level of the other protein (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Rab8 goes to the cilium in Rab10KO cells, as in wild type cells.
source: In addition, Rab8 goes to the cilium in Rab10KO cells, as in wild type cells.
evidence: This claim is based on observations from the experimental data.

claim: Phosphorylation of Rab proteins by LRRK2 interferes with their ability to bind to numerous, cognate effector proteins.
source: Phosphorylation of Rab proteins by LRRK2 has been shown to interfere with their ability of to bind to numerous, cognate effector proteins (Steger et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Steger et al., 2016.

claim: The non-phosphorylatable, threonine to alanine (TA) mutations in both Rab8A and Rab10 failed to reverse their respective ciliation phenotypes observed in knockout cells.
source: The non-phosphorylatable, threonine to alanine (TA) mutations in both Rab8A and Rab10 failed to reverse their respective ciliation phenotypes observed in knockout cells (Table 1), indicating that they are non-functional.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data summarized in Table 1.

claim: Rab8A-TA was more concentrated over the Golgi and not seen in cilia.
source: Light microscopy of A549 cells expressing these mutants showed that unlike wild type Rab8A protein, Rab8A-TA was more concentrated over the Golgi and not seen in cilia
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental observations from light microscopy.

claim: Rab8A-TE was more dispersed than the wild type protein and may aggregate upon expression in HEK293T cells.
source: Rab8A-TE was more dispersed than the wild type protein and may aggregate upon expression in HEK293T cells.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental observations from light microscopy, with speculation about aggregation.

claim: Rab10-TE was much more concentrated on the Golgi than the wild type protein.
source: Rab10-TE was much more concentrated on the Golgi than the wild type protein and Rab10-TA was entirely cytosolic (Figure 2A)
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Rab10-TA was entirely cytosolic.
source: Rab10-TE was much more concentrated on the Golgi than the wild type protein and Rab10-TA was entirely cytosolic (Figure 2A), as confirmed by membrane fractionation after expression in HEK293T cells (Figure 2B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A and 2B.

claim: Neither Rab8A-TE nor Rab10-TA mutants are good substrates for Rab geranylgeranyl transferase.
source: In vitro experiments using biotin-geranyl pyrophosphate as substrate confirmed that neither Rab8A-TE nor Rab10-TA mutants are good substrates for Rab geranylgeranyl transferase (Figure 2C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Rab8A-TE and Rab10-TE failed to show enhanced interaction with GFP-RILPL1 protein.
source: Finally, unlike the phosphorylated versions of Rab8A or Rab10 proteins (Steger et al., 2017), Rab8A-TE and Rab10-TE failed to show enhanced interaction with GFP-RILPL1 protein (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1 and citation to Steger et al., 2017.

claim: The TA and TE mutants do not reflect the desired states and should not be used in future experiments exploring the consequences of Rab8A and Rab10 phosphorylation.
source: This is a very important caution—the TA and TE mutants do not reflect the desired states and should not be used in future experiments exploring the consequences of Rab8A and Rab10 phosphorylation.
evidence: This claim is an inference based on the experimental data showing that these mutants are non-functional.

claim: Rab10 is phosphorylated in cells transfected with LRRK2 kinase.
source: Rab10 is phosphorylated in cells transfected with LRRK2 kinase (Steger et al., 2016; Purlyte et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Steger et al., 2016 and Purlyte et al., 2018.

claim: Approximately 80% of cells expressing exogenous LRRK2 showed total Rab10 concentrated over a perinuclear cluster.
source: After 24 hr,~80% of cells expressing exogenous LRRK2 showed total Rab10 concentrated over a perinuclear cluster (Figure 3A,B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A and 3B.

claim: The strongest pRab10 signal was detected in the perinuclear region together with total Rab10 staining.
source: Furthermore, labeling of LRRK2 expressing cells using a commercial anti-phosphoT73 Rab10-specific antibody revealed pRab10 staining only in LRRK2 co-expressing cells; the strongest pRab10 signal was also detected in the perinuclear region together with total Rab10 staining (Figure 3C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: pRab10 localized adjacent to centrioles labeled with Centrin-3.
source: pRab10 localized adjacent to centrioles labeled with Centrin-3, and co-localized with perinuclear transferrin receptor (TfR)-containing membranes (Figure 3C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: pRab10 co-localized with perinuclear transferrin receptor (TfR)-containing membranes.
source: pRab10 localized adjacent to centrioles labeled with Centrin-3, and co-localized with perinuclear transferrin receptor (TfR)-containing membranes (Figure 3C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: RILPL1 interacts preferentially with the phosphorylated forms of Rab8A and Rab10.
source: As noted earlier, RILPL1 interacts preferentially with the phosphorylated forms of Rab8A and Rab10 (Steger et al., 2017); Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Steger et al., 2017 and experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: The clustered pRab10 co-localized perfectly with RILPL1 in the peri-centriolar region in HEK293T cells co-transfected with RILPL1-GFP and LRRK2.
source: In HEK293T cells co-transfected with RILPL1-GFP and LRRK2, the clustered pRab10 co-localized perfectly with RILPL1 in the peri-centriolar region.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental observations from microscopy.

claim: RILPL1 binds to pRab10 in cells.
source: This strong co-localization supports the conclusion that RILPL1 binds to pRab10 in cells.
evidence: This claim is an inference based on the co-localization data.

claim: RILPL1 has been shown to associate with the mother centriole that becomes the basal body that nucleates the primary cilium.
source: RILPL1 has been shown to associate with the mother centriole that becomes the basal body that nucleates the primary cilium (Schaub and Stearns, 2013); RILPL1's C-terminal half is needed for this localization.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Schaub and Stearns, 2013.

claim: RILPL1's C-terminal half is needed for its localization to the mother centriole.
source: RILPL1 has been shown to associate with the mother centriole that becomes the basal body that nucleates the primary cilium (Schaub and Stearns, 2013); RILPL1's C-terminal half is needed for this localization.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Schaub and Stearns, 2013.

claim: RILPL1-GFP co-localized with CEP164, a marker of the mother centriole.
source: We confirmed mother centriole localization of RILPL1 in A549 cells (Figure 3—figure supplement 1); RILPL1-GFP co-localized with CEP164, a marker of the mother centriole.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: RILPL1 influences the removal of signaling receptors from primary cilia.
source: Previous work also indicated that RILPL1 influences the removal of signaling receptors from primary cilia (Schaub and Stearns, 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Schaub and Stearns, 2013.

claim: Primary cilia form in G1 of the cell cycle and disassemble before mitosis.
source: Primary cilia form in G1 of the cell cycle and disassemble before mitosis.
evidence: This claim is based on established knowledge about the cell cycle regulation of cilia.

claim: Endogenous RILPL1 co-localized with Rab10 at the base of primary cilia in RPE cells that had been induced to form cilia by serum starvation.
source: In RPE cells that had been induced to form cilia by serum starvation, endogenous RILPL1 co-localized with Rab10 at the base of primary cilia, identified by staining with anti-Arl13B antibodies (Figure 4A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: A similar localization of RILPL1 and Rab10 was seen in ciliated, primary rat astrocytes.
source: A similar localization was also seen in ciliated, primary rat astrocytes (Figure 4B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: When RILPL1 expression was decreased in HEK293T cells using a lentiviral shRNA, perinuclear clustering of pRab10 decreased.
source: When RILPL1 expression was decreased in HEK293T cells using a lentiviral shRNA, perinuclear clustering of pRab10 decreased and that phenotype was corrected upon RILPL1-GFP expression (Figure 4D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: Perinuclear pRab10 clustering increased upon exogenous RILPL1 expression.
source: Indeed, perinuclear pRab10 clustering increased upon exogenous RILPL1 expression (Figure 4D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: Overexpression of the C-terminal half of RILPL1 (RILPL1-C-GFP) dispersed pRab10 localization.
source: Overexpression of the C-terminal half of RILPL1 (RILPL1-C-GFP) dispersed pRab10 localization, whereas expression of the N-terminal half (RILPL1-N-GFP) had the same effect as the full length protein (Figure 4C,E).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4C and 4E.

claim: Expression of the N-terminal half of RILPL1 (RILPL1-N-GFP) had the same effect as the full length protein on pRab10 localization.
source: Overexpression of the C-terminal half of RILPL1 (RILPL1-C-GFP) dispersed pRab10 localization, whereas expression of the N-terminal half (RILPL1-N-GFP) had the same effect as the full length protein (Figure 4C,E).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4C and 4E.

claim: Overexpression of the RILPL1 C-terminal half interferes with RILPL1 localization and dominantly blocks primary cilia formation.
source: Previous work showed that overexpression of the RILPL1 C-terminal half interferes with RILPL1 localization and this region localizes RILPL1 to the centriole and dominantly blocks primary cilia formation (Schaub and Stearns, 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Schaub and Stearns, 2013.

claim: The RILPL1 N-terminus interacts with pRab10 in pericentriolar membranes.
source: Altogether, these data suggest that the RILPL1 N-terminus interacts with pRab10 in pericentriolar membranes
evidence: This claim is an inference based on the experimental data showing that the N-terminal half has the same effect as full-length RILPL1.

claim: Overexpression of the RILPL1 C-terminus dominantly interferes with cilia formation, perhaps by competing for interactions that localize pRab10 and RILPL1 to the pericentriolar compartment.
source: overexpression of the C-terminus dominantly interferes with cilia formation, perhaps by competing for interactions that localize pRab10 and RILPL1 to that cellular compartment.
evidence: This claim is speculation based on the experimental observations.

claim: Even in the absence of RILPL1, some pRab10 localized to the pericentriolar region.
source: Nevertheless, even in the absence of RILPL1, some pRab10 localized to the pericentriolar region.
evidence: This claim is based on experimental observations.

claim: Residual pRab10 localization in the absence of RILPL1 may be due to association with the related RILPL2 protein still present in these cells and/or to other proteins.
source: This may be due to association with the related RILPL2 protein still present in these cells and/or to other proteins.
evidence: This claim is speculation about the mechanism.

claim: RILPL1 KO A549 cells had a less focused distribution of pRab10 and showed additional punctate structures in the cytosol compared to parental A549 cells.
source: While LRRK2 transfected, parental A549 cells displayed most pRab10 in a peri-nuclear cluster, RILPL1 KO A549 cells had a less focused distribution of pRab10 and showed additional punctate structures in the cytosol (Figure 4F–H).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4F-H.

claim: RILPL1 enhances pRab10 clustering on pericentriolar membranes.
source: These data support the conclusion that RILPL1 enhances pRab10 clustering on pericentriolar membranes.
evidence: This claim is an inference based on the experimental data showing altered pRab10 distribution in RILPL1 KO cells.

claim: Knockout of RILPL1 in A549 cells increased the percentage of cells that contained primary cilia.
source: Knockout of RILPL1 in A549 cells increased the percentage of cells that contained primary cilia, and the length of the cilia also increased (Figure 5A,B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5A and 5B.

claim: Knockout of RILPL1 in A549 cells increased the length of the cilia.
source: Knockout of RILPL1 in A549 cells increased the percentage of cells that contained primary cilia, and the length of the cilia also increased (Figure 5A,B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5A and 5B.

claim: The effect of RILPL1 knockout on ciliation was abrogated upon expression of exogenous RILPL1.
source: This effect was abrogated upon expression of exogenous RILPL1 (Figure 5C), indicating that exogenous RILPL1 suppresses primary cilia formation, in wild type cells and in cells lacking RILPL1 protein.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Exogenous RILPL1 suppresses primary cilia formation in wild type cells and in cells lacking RILPL1 protein.
source: This effect was abrogated upon expression of exogenous RILPL1 (Figure 5C), indicating that exogenous RILPL1 suppresses primary cilia formation, in wild type cells and in cells lacking RILPL1 protein.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5C.
